at: flat on his back in the grass where he hatched
alt: Six young Gaya kings laughing in the grass on Turtle Peak while the nine chiefs stand over them
scene: Turtle Peak, the next spring: six young Gaya kings in the grass on the hilltop where they hatched. Ijinasi flat on his back howling with laughter, Suro sitting up laughing last with a hand over his face, four other young kings doubled over around them; the nine grey-robed chiefs standing behind, the only ones not laughing. Crane shot looking down on the ring of bodies in the grass, storm-break dusk over the southern sea behind the peak, one low gold shaft. Heewon style, 2:1.

alt: Suro on his knees among scattered jade, holding up the last bead to the Mahan girl as she keeps dancing
scene: The queen-contest feast in Golden Gaya's timber hall at night: the Mahan chief's daughter, bare-throated, still dancing in the middle of the floor while jade beads scatter across the boards and chiefs scramble under the tables; Suro in a plain coat on his knees at her feet, a wine jar in one hand, holding the last green bead up to her. Worm's-eye from the floor between the beads, oil lamp on the boards beside the lens, her shadow climbing the wall. Implied tension only. Heewon style, 2:1.

at: Most of it lands on his feet
alt: The Tamla diver wrings her wet hair over the disguised king's feet, holding his eyes
scene: Gaya beach at dusk during the queen contest: the Tamla diver, soaked, standing close in front of Suro in a plain coat in the crowd, wringing seawater out of her long hair so it falls on his feet, holding his eyes; Ijinasi in a second plain coat at his shoulder, grinning. Low over-the-shoulder from behind Suro, wet sand reflecting one low sun break. Heewon style, 2:1.
